title: Posterior Convergence without Force Convergence: Resolution-Stable Sampling for Rough Bayesian Inverse Problems
summary: Bayesian targets may converge under model refinement even when the exact sensitivities used by gradient-based samplers do not. We study this probability--sensitivity mismatch and its consequences for Metropolized Hamiltonian proposals. A vanishing-amplitude wiggly-energy model first gives the basic analytic obstruction: the potential perturbation tends to zero while its classical derivative is of order $r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon$.
